reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Reporting one number without saying which region.
Applying it to non-vascular white matter disease without comment.
name: Fazekas Scale for White Matter Hyperintensities

version.label: Fazekas scale (Fazekas et al. 1987)
version.detail: Periventricular (0–3) and deep white matter (0–3) graded separately on T2/FLAIR MRI. The deep white matter grade is the one most often reported alone.

purpose: Grades the extent of white matter T2 hyperintensities.
intendedPopulation: Adults with brain MRI (T2/FLAIR), e.g. in cerebrovascular disease or cognitive assessment.

options.label: Irregular periventricular signal extending into deep white matter

resultStates.label: No white matter hyperintensities
resultStates.summary: No periventricular or deep white matter hyperintensities graded at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Grades the T2/FLAIR appearance only; it does not exclude other pathology.

resultStates.label: Deep grade 0–1
resultStates.summary: Absent or punctate deep white matter hyperintensities (periventricular graded separately).

resultStates.label: Deep grade 2
resultStates.summary: Beginning confluence of deep white matter hyperintensities.

resultStates.label: Deep grade 3
resultStates.summary: Large confluent deep white matter hyperintensities.
resultStates.detail: Interpret with age, vascular risk factors and the clinical question; assess for other causes of white matter change.

clinicalContext.text: A widely used visual rating of white matter hyperintensities, often presumed of vascular origin in older adults.

clinicalInsights.text: Report both grades; the deep grade is often quoted alone (e.g. 'Fazekas 2').

limitations.text: Visual, ordinal rating with ceiling effects; insensitive to small change.

limitations: Depends on sequence and field strength.

confounders.effect: Produces hyperintensities of a different cause.
Some hyperintensity is common with ageing.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: The cause of the white matter change.

guideSections.what: Separate 0–3 grades for periventricular and deep white matter hyperintensities.
guideSections.whenToUse: MRI reporting in cerebrovascular disease and cognitive impairment.
guideSections.howToPerform: On FLAIR/T2, grade the periventricular pattern (caps, halo, extension) and the deep white matter pattern (punctate, beginning confluence, confluent).
guideSections.clinicalContext: An imaging descriptor, interpreted with age and clinical context.

sources.citation: Fazekas F, Chawluk JB, Alavi A, Hurtig HI, Zimmerman RA. MR signal abnormalities at 1.5 T in Alzheimer's dementia and normal aging. AJR Am J Roentgenol. 1987;149(2):351-356.
